arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Sauer opened by stating that deceit or gross negligence in financial transactions is cause for removal. He described Cook submitting mortgage applications for two properties in a two-week period in 2021. He then argued the district court lacked jurisdiction to enter the preliminary injunction under the Court's holding in Sawyer.
Clement opened by describing the Federal Reserve as a uniquely structured entity with a distinct historical tradition.

Sotomayor pressed on the scope of the D. C. Circuit's decision. She asked whether it addressed the definition of cause, including pre-office conduct and the required nexus. She noted the unprecedented nature of the removal. She said keeping Cook does not thwart any right Trump has to run the department because he conceded he has none.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Trump's side wants Cook removed. They say her pre-office conduct shows deceit or gross negligence.
Cook's side wants to keep her position. They say the Federal Reserve's structure limits presidential removal power.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Sauer said the statutory standard is not limited to in-office misconduct. He argued Congress did not adopt that limitation here.
Clement said the Federal Reserve is a uniquely structured entity. He pointed to its distinct historical tradition.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked whether the D.C. Circuit decided anything beyond the constitutional question.

Justice Thomas questioned whether the Federal Reserve is an executive branch agency at all. He said this is an antecedent point to the removal question. He asked on what basis the Court should conclude the president has removal authority over it. Sotomayor added that the unprecedented nature of the removal reflects what the president did, not what Cook did.
